statement: The category and its localization: There is a category $\Cathot_\U$ with the same objects as $\Cat_\U$ and \[ \Hom_{\Cathot}(X,K)=\pi _0\Fun(X,K). \] Here two functors represent the same morphism precisely when they are joined by a finite zigzag of natural transformations, whose orientations may vary. The class $\overline\W_\infty$ consists of the classes of functors in $\W_\infty$. The functor $\varphi:\Cathot\to\Hot$, $[f]\mapsto[Bf]$, is a localization at this class, and $\varphi[f]$ is invertible precisely when $f\in\W_\infty$. The identification $\Hot\simeq\Ho(\Spc_\U)$ uses weak homotopy types of spaces, including the empty space.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, statement A.1 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 3

statement: The specified fundamental-localizer convention: The class $\W_\infty$ satisfies Loc(1)--(3) as stated on the first page. For any fundamental localizer in that convention, localization identifies naturally transformed functors. In particular, the categorical quotient used in A.1 is compatible with the variance of those axioms.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, statement A.2 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 3

statement: Proposition 1 is a conditional formal theorem: Let $L:C\to D$ and $R:D\to C$ be functors between locally small categories, let $L\dashv R$, and suppose $R$ is fully faithful. Write $\eta:\id_C\to RL$ and $\epsilon:LR\to\id_D$ for the unit and counit, and $W_L=\{u\mid Lu\text{ is invertible}\}$. For $K\in C$, the following conditions are equivalent: $\Hom_C(-,K)$ inverts $W_L$; it inverts every $\eta_X$; precomposition with $\eta_K$ is bijective; $\eta_K$ has a retraction; $\eta_K$ is invertible; $K$ is in the essential image of $R$; and the canonical map \[ \Hom_C(X,K)\longrightarrow\Hom_D(LX,LK) \] is bijective for every $X\in C$. If $H':D^{\op}\to\Set$ and $H=H' L^{\op}$, then $H$ is representable if and only if $H'$ is representable. In that event their representing objects satisfy $K\cong RK'$ and $K'\cong LK$, compatibly with the specified representations.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, statement A.3 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 4

statement: Ind-categories and Proposition 2: Use one fixed auxiliary universe for the filtered indexing categories. For $I,J$ small filtered, $K:I\to C$ and $T:J\to C$, put \[ h_K(X)=\colim_{i\in I}\Hom_C(X,K_i),\qquad \Hom_{\Ind C}(K,T)=\lim_{i\in I}\colim_{j\in J}\Hom_C(K_i,T_j). \] The association $K\mapsto h_K$ is fully faithful. Under the hypotheses of A.3, $\Ind L\dashv\Ind R$ and $\Ind R$ is fully faithful. For an ind-object $K$, the following are equivalent: $h_K$ inverts $W_L$; it inverts all $\eta_X$ for $X\in C$; the unit $K\to(\Ind R)(\Ind L)K$ is invertible; $K$ belongs to the essential image of $\Ind R$; and the canonical comparison \[ h_K(X)\longrightarrow \Hom_{\Ind D}(LX,(\Ind L)K) \] is bijective for every $X\in C$. These are precisely the valid, typed contents of V ms.~40--42.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, statement A.4 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 4

statement: The precise model-category mapping formula: Thomason's model category has weak equivalences $\W_\infty$ and fibrations detected by $\operatorname{Ex}^2N$. Its adjunction \[ c\operatorname{Sd}^2:\mathbf{sSet}\rightleftarrows\Cat: \operatorname{Ex}^2N \] is a Quillen equivalence. Choose a fibrant replacement $K\to RK$ in this model category. Put $QX=c\operatorname{Sd}^2NX$. The composite last-vertex map gives a natural weak equivalence $q_X:QX\to X$, and $QX$ is cofibrant. There are natural bijections \[ [BX,BK]\cong\pi_0\Map_{\mathbf{sSet}}(NX,\operatorname{Ex}^2NRK) \cong\Fun(QX,RK)_0/\sim_T . \] Here $\Fun(QX,RK)_0$ is the set of functors, and $\sim_T$ is generated by endpoint restrictions of functors $c\operatorname{Sd}^2(NX\times\Delta^1)\to RK$. For any cofibrant replacement $Q'X\to X$, one may equivalently use $\Hom_{\Cat}(Q'X,RK)$ modulo model-category homotopy. The displayed explicit relation specifies that homotopy; it does not silently replace it by a different cylinder relation.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, statement A.5 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 5
notes: Exact model-cylinder relation; the source is replaced and the target is fibrant.

statement: A fibrant target does not suffice: The assertion that $\pi_0\Fun(X,P)\to[BX,BP]$ is always a bijection for a Thomason-fibrant $P$ is false, even for a finite $X$. The assertion that $\Fun(X,P)$ is always Thomason-fibrant is also false, even for a finite $X$ and a countable fibrant $P$.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, statement A.6 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 5
notes: Two distinct counterexamples; finite ingredient checks in a_finite_checks.py.

statement: Descent of ind-representability needs no right adjoint: Let $L:C\to D$ be any localization, and let $H=\colim_{i\in I}h_{K_i}$ be a small filtered colimit of representable presheaves. If $H\cong H' L^{\op}$, then the canonical comparison identifies \[ H'\cong\colim_{i\in I}\Hom_D(-,LK_i). \] For a single representing object, it follows that $h_K$ inverts the localized class if and only if its canonical comparison with $\Hom_D(L-,LK)$ is bijective. This assertion, and not a reflection, is sufficient for the descent of the manuscript's external Hom ind-objects.
where_proved: sections/A.tex, statement A.7 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 6

statement: What a sufficiently large group sees in a small category: Let $K$ be a $\U$-small category and let $G$ be a $\U$-small group such that every group homomorphism $G\longrightarrow H$ is trivial whenever $|H|\leq |\Mor K|$. The constant-functor map and evaluation map \[ \delta_K:K\longrightarrow\Fun(\mathsf B G,K),\qquad \operatorname{ev}_*: \Fun(\mathsf B G,K)\longrightarrow K \] are mutually inverse isomorphisms of categories. Consequently the map \[ p^*:\Hom_{\Cathot}(e,K)\longrightarrow \Hom_{\Cathot}(\mathsf B G,K),\qquad p:\mathsf B G\longrightarrow e, \] is a bijection. Both assertions are natural in $K$ among categories whose automorphism groups receive only trivial homomorphisms from $G$.
where_proved: sections/BC.tex, statement B.1 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 7
notes: Includes empty categories and noninvertible endomorphisms.

statement: The finite Schur-multiplier input: For a finite set $F$ with $|F|\geq8$, \[ H_1(\operatorname{Alt}(F);\Z)=0, \qquad H_2(\operatorname{Alt}(F);\Z)\cong\Z/2. \] If $a,b,c,d$ are distinct elements of $F$, the commuting permutations $x=(ab)(cd)$ and $y=(ac)(bd)$ define a torus class \[ t_F=[x\mid y]-[y\mid x]\in H_2(\operatorname{Alt}(F);\Z) \] which generates this group. In particular, inclusions between finite alternating groups on sets containing these four elements and having at least eight elements carry generator to generator.
where_proved: sections/BC.tex, statement B.2 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 7
notes: Finite upper bound is an imported classical theorem; transition maps checked using a fixed generator; exact Clifford algebra check attached.

statement: Finitary alternating groups at every infinite cardinal: Let $\Omega$ be an infinite $\U$-small set and let $A_\Omega=\operatorname{Alt}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\Omega)$ be the group of even permutations with finite support. Then \[ |A_\Omega|=|\Omega|,\qquad A_\Omega\text{ is nonabelian simple},\qquad H_1(A_\Omega;\Z)=0,\quad H_2(A_\Omega;\Z)=\Z/2. \] Every homomorphism from $A_\Omega$ to a group of cardinality strictly less than $|\Omega|$ is trivial.
where_proved: sections/BC.tex, statement B.3 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 8
notes: Simplicity proved with fresh-point commutator; bar complexes give filtered homology colimit with verified transition maps.

statement: The asserted right adjoint and the first proposed envelope: There is no $\U$-small category $K$ representing \[ X\longmapsto [BX,K(\Z/2,2)] \quad\text{on }\Cathot^{\op}. \] Consequently $\varphi:\Cathot\to\Hot$ has no right adjoint, fully faithful or otherwise. The assertion at V~ms.~37 and the unrestricted Thomason--Kan-envelope construction at V~ms.~42--43 are false.
where_proved: sections/BC.tex, statement B.4 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 8
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: V ms.37--43; III-V companion unproved reflection block
notes: Refutes existence of any right adjoint, not only a fully faithful one.

statement: A simple overgroup with a prescribed infinite cardinality: Let $H$ be a $\U$-small group and let $\lambda$ be an infinite $\U$-cardinal with $|H|\leq\lambda$. There is an injective homomorphism $H\hookrightarrow S$ into a nonabelian simple $\U$-small group $S$ with $|S|=\lambda$.
where_proved: sections/BC.tex, statement B.5 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 9
notes: Explicit free-product word w=[g,t][g,t^2] and HNN relations put every h in normal closure of g; cardinal bound checked.

statement: An acyclic overgroup without a cardinal increase: For every infinite $\U$-small group $H$ there is an injective homomorphism $H\hookrightarrow M(H)$ with \[ |M(H)|=|H|,\qquad \widetilde H_i(BM(H);\Z)=0 \quad\text{for every }i\geq0. \] For a finite $H$, the same construction gives a countable overgroup.
where_proved: sections/BC.tex, statement B.6 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 10
notes: Mitosis construction and field-homology annihilation proof supplied.

statement: Acyclic simple overgroups of arbitrary size: For every group $H$ and every infinite $\U$-cardinal $\lambda\geq\max(|H|,\aleph_0)$ there is a monomorphism of groups $i:H\hookrightarrow A$ such that $A$ is nonabelian simple, $|A|=\lambda$, and $BA$ is integrally acyclic.
where_proved: sections/BC.tex, statement B.7 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 10
notes: Alternating injective simple and acyclic envelopes; no priority claimed.

statement: Groups invisible to smaller groups and mapping to spheres: For every integer $n\geq2$ and every infinite $\U$-cardinal $\lambda$ there is a $\U$-small group $G_{n,\lambda}$ and a pointed continuous map of CW models \[ q_{n,\lambda}:BG_{n,\lambda}\longrightarrow S^n \] such that $|G_{n,\lambda}|=\lambda$, the map $q_{n,\lambda}$ induces isomorphisms on integral homology in all degrees, and every homomorphism from $G_{n,\lambda}$ to a group of cardinality less than $\lambda$ is trivial. The group $G_{n,\lambda}$ is perfect. It is not asserted to be simple.
where_proved: sections/BC.tex, statement B.8 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 11
notes: Iterated amalgamated doubles over acyclic simple envelopes; group need not itself be simple.

statement: The target condition needed to use these homology equivalences: Let $u:A\to B$ be a pointed integral homology equivalence between connected CW spaces, and let $Z$ be a pointed simply connected CW space. Precomposition induces a weak equivalence of derived pointed mapping spaces \[ u^*:\Map_*(B,Z)\longrightarrow\Map_*(A,Z). \] In particular it induces a bijection $[B,Z]_*\to[A,Z]_*$.
where_proved: sections/BC.tex, statement B.9 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 12
notes: Full Postnikov mapping-space argument handles infinite towers and avoids phantom-map inference.

statement: Essential maps from arbitrarily large groups for every higher type: Let $Y$ be a $\U$-small homotopy type with a point $y$ and a nonzero element $\alpha\in\pi_n(Y,y)$ for some $n\geq2$. For every infinite $\U$-cardinal $\lambda$, the group $G_{n,\lambda}$ of B.8 has no nontrivial homomorphism to any group of cardinality less than $\lambda$ and admits a map $BG_{n,\lambda}\to Y$ which is not freely homotopic to a constant map. Thus this assertion holds for every homotopy type that is not a $1$-type, including every simply connected noncontractible homotopy type.
where_proved: sections/BC.tex, statement B.10 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 12
notes: Universal-cover lifting proves non-nullness for arbitrary nontrivial pi_1 action.

statement: The full negative representability statement: For every $\U$-small homotopy type $Y$ which is not a $1$-type, the presheaf $X\mapsto[BX,Y]$ on $\Cathot$ is not representable by a $\U$-small category. No connectedness assumption on $Y$ is needed.
where_proved: sections/BC.tex, statement B.11 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 13
notes: Naturality of constant-map square handles disconnected targets and infinite component sets.

statement: Groupoids are local, with the canonical comparison: For every $\U$-small category $X$ and $\U$-small groupoid $G$, the canonical map \[ \pi_0\Fun(X,G)\longrightarrow[BX,BG] \] is a bijection, natural in both variables. More precisely, \[ N\Fun(X,G)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(NX,NG) \] is an isomorphism of simplicial sets, and the right side is a derived mapping space. Restriction along $\eta_X$ is an isomorphism of categories $\Fun(\Pi_1X,G)\to\Fun(X,G)$.
where_proved: sections/BC.tex, statement C.1 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 13
notes: NFun(X,G) is exactly the Kan derived simplicial mapping space.

statement: Classification of all representable homotopy types: A $\U$-small homotopy type $Y$ has its presheaf $X\mapsto[BX,Y]$ represented on $\Cathot$ by a $\U$-small category if and only if $Y$ is a $1$-type. If $Y$ is a $1$-type, a fundamental groupoid $G_Y$ represents it. Every other representing category is isomorphic to $G_Y$ in $\Cathot$, and its classifying space is isomorphic to $Y$ in $\Hot$. This is a complete affirmative answer to Lead~2's representability conjecture.
where_proved: sections/BC.tex, statement C.2 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 14
notes: Includes empty and disconnected types; specified universal element is a weak equivalence in Hot.

statement: Classification of local categories: For a $\U$-small category $K$, the following conditions are equivalent: the canonical function $\pi_0\Fun(X,K)\to[BX,BK]$ is bijective for every $\U$-small $X$; the category $K$ is isomorphic in $\Cathot$ to a groupoid; and the canonical functor $\eta_K:K\to\Pi_1K$ is an isomorphism in $\Cathot$. In particular every local $K$ has $BK$ a $1$-type. Conversely, for a category with $BK$ a $1$-type, localness is equivalent to being isomorphic in $\Cathot$ to its groupoidification. The hypothesis that $BK$ is a $1$-type alone is insufficient.
where_proved: sections/BC.tex, statement C.3 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 14
notes: Localness forces a 1-type; the converse from nerve 1-type alone fails.

statement: The reflector is fundamental groupoidification: Let $\mathcal L\subset\Cathot$ be the full subcategory of local objects. It is reflective. After identifying it with groupoids modulo natural isomorphism, its reflector is \[ \Pi_1:\Cathot\longrightarrow\operatorname{Ho}(\mathrm{Grpd}), \qquad \Pi_1\dashv I, \] where $I$ is the full inclusion and the unit is $[\eta_X]$. This reflector inverts exactly those functors that induce a bijection on components and isomorphisms on fundamental groups at every basepoint. Its unit is in $W_\infty$ precisely when $BX$ is a $1$-type. In particular this reflection does not supply the nonexistent right adjoint to $\varphi:\Cathot\to\Hot$.
where_proved: sections/BC.tex, statement C.4 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 15
notes: This reflector inverts W_1, not merely W_infty; unit is W_infty exactly for 1-types.

statement: Coreflectivity, and the weaker converse from the classifying space: The inclusion $I:\mathcal L\hookrightarrow\Cathot$ has no right adjoint. Moreover, a category with contractible classifying space need not be local.
where_proved: sections/BC.tex, statement C.5 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 15
notes: Infinite fence and discrete N source give a uniform-length obstruction; finite truncation checks attached.

statement: Thomason fibrancy is not the manuscript's localness: It is false that every Thomason-fibrant category is local in the sense of C.3. There is no change of target by a $W_\infty$-equivalence that makes a homotopy type with nonzero higher homotopy groups into a local category.
where_proved: sections/BC.tex, statement C.6 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 16
notes: Fibrant replacement of a category of type S^2 has a higher type and is not local.

statement: Exact bounded representability: Let $Y$ be a $\U$-small Kan complex and let $\lambda\in\U$ be an infinite cardinal with $|Y|\leq\lambda$, where size counts simplices in all degrees. There is a $\U$-small category $K_\lambda(Y)$ and a natural transformation \[ \theta_{X,\lambda}:\pi_0\Fun(X,K_\lambda(Y))\longrightarrow[NX,Y] \qquad (X\in\Cat_\U) \] which is bijective whenever $|\Mor X|\leq\lambda$. One can take $|\Mor K_\lambda(Y)|\leq2^\lambda$. Consequently, for every infinite $\kappa\in\U$, the functor in Part D(i), on categories with fewer than $\kappa$ arrows, is represented by a small category after allowing the representing category to exceed the test bound.
where_proved: sections/D.tex, statement D.1 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 16
notes: Explicit at-most-2^lambda arrow bound; natural comparison proved for all sources within lambda.

statement: Finite targets are not enough in the test examples: On the full category of finite categories, neither $X\mapsto[BX,S^2]$ nor $X\mapsto[BX,K(C_2,2)]$ has a finite representing category in $\Cathot$. Both have small, generally infinite, representing categories by D.1. For $K(C_2,2)$ and an uncountable limit cardinal $\kappa$, a representative for all tests with fewer than $\kappa$ arrows cannot itself have fewer than $\kappa$ arrows.
where_proved: sections/D.tex, statement D.2 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 17

statement: Finite categories always give a filtered ind-representation: Let $\mathcal C_f$ be a skeleton of finite categories in $\Cathot$, with all functors modulo natural-transformation zigzags as morphisms. For every $\U$-small homotopy type $Y$, put $F_Y(C)=[BC,Y]$. The category of elements $\mathcal E_Y$ of $F_Y|_{\mathcal C_f}$ is a small filtered category, and \[ F_Y|_{\mathcal C_f}\cong \colim_{(C,c)\in\mathcal E_Y}\Hom_{\Cathot}(-,C)|_{\mathcal C_f}. \] Thus Part D(ii) has an affirmative answer for filtered ind-representability by finite categories. The assertion does not require that a finite category have homotopy-finite nerve.
where_proved: sections/D.tex, statement D.3 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 18
notes: Index is arbitrary small filtered; no unsupported strictification of a general filtered Cathot diagram.

statement: The exact sequential criterion: For $Y\in\Hot_\U$, the restriction $F_Y|_{\mathcal C_f}$ is a colimit of a sequence of representables by finite categories if and only if $[BC,Y]$ is countable for every finite category $C$. Such a sequence may be represented by actual functors of finite categories. Its colimit $K$ in $\Cat$ is a countable locally finite category and represents $F_Y$ on finite tests. Conversely, every countable locally finite representing category supplies such a sequence. Here a category is locally finite when each finitely generated subcategory has finitely many arrows.
where_proved: sections/D.tex, statement D.4 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 18
notes: Sequential strictification only; the colimit is locally finite without requiring injective transitions.

statement: The Eilenberg--Mac Lane sequential example: For $Y=K(C_2,2)$, the restriction to finite categories is ind-representable by a sequence of finite categories and representable by a countable locally finite category, although it is not representable on all $\Cathot_\U$ by any $\U$-small category.
where_proved: sections/D.tex, statement D.5 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 19

statement: The sequential two-sphere test: The remaining exact question in Part D(ii) for $Y=S^2$ is whether $[BC,S^2]$ is countable for every finite category $C$. By D.4 this is equivalent to sequential ind-representability by finite categories; it is also equivalent to representability on finite tests by a countable locally finite category. General filtered ind-representability and ordinary small representability on these tests are already proved in D.3 and D.1. No assertion of sequential representability for $S^2$ is certified here.
where_proved: sections/D.tex, statement D.6 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 19
notes: Open in this audit; not a claim of absence of a result in the literature.

statement: The unbounded cardinal-indexed representation: There is a compatible choice of the categories $K_\lambda(Y)$ for $\lambda\geq\max(\aleph_0,|Y|)$ and inclusion functors for increasing $\lambda$, such that, in the larger universe $\V$, \[ [B-,Y]\cong\colim_{\lambda\in\operatorname{Card}(\U),\ \lambda\geq\max(\aleph_0,|Y|)} \Hom_{\Cathot_\U}(-,K_\lambda(Y)). \] The indexing poset is filtered, $\V$-small, and unbounded in the $\U$-cardinals. Alternatively $F_Y$ is a $\V$-small filtered colimit over its category of elements on all $\Cathot_\U$.
where_proved: sections/D.tex, statement D.7 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 19

statement: Why the larger index is necessary: If $Y$ has a component with a nonzero homotopy group in degree at least two, $F_Y$ on all $\Cathot_\U$ is not a $\U$-small colimit of representables, even without requiring the colimit to be filtered. If $Y$ is a 1-type it is representable by its fundamental groupoid. Thus, for the global functor, enlarging the index universe in D.7 is essential exactly outside the 1-types.
where_proved: sections/D.tex, statement D.8 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 20
notes: Rules out any U-small indexing category, not merely filtered ones.

statement: The bounded conclusion also follows from Raptis's model structures: Let $\mu\in\U$ be a regular infinite cardinal. There is a model structure $\Cat_{I(\mu)}$ with weak equivalences $\W_\infty$ in which every $\mu$-presentable category is cofibrant. If $K\to R_\mu K$ is a fibrant replacement in this structure, then the canonical comparison \[ \pi_0\Fun(X,R_\mu K)\longrightarrow[BX,BK] \] is a bijection for every $\mu$-presentable $X$, in particular for every $X$ with fewer than $\mu$ arrows. Thus bounded representability is also a consequence of a known model structure; the construction in D.1 additionally gives its explicit size bound and compatible cardinal filtration.
where_proved: sections/D_model.tex, statement D.9 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 20
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: Part D(i); Raptis bounded model structures
notes: Known existence route; explicit bounded cardinal construction is D.1.

statement: V ms.~37--44: the permissible replacements: The formal propositions on V ms.~37--42 remain theorems with the adjunction hypothesis in A.3--A.4. Their specialization to a right adjoint of $\varphi$ is refuted by B.4. For an individual category $K$, a local category weakly equivalent to $K$ exists if and only if $BK$ is a 1-type; in that case $\eta_K:K\to\Pi_1K$ is such a weak equivalence. For arbitrary $K$, a Thomason fibrant replacement exists, with the mapping property of A.5. For a fixed bounded family of sources, D.1 gives a target that represents the required Hom-functor on that family. For a weak-equivalence-invariant ind-represented functor, A.7 gives its descended ind-object in $\Hot$ without any envelope.
where_proved: sections/E.tex, statement E.1 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 21

statement: V ms.~45: the uniform-stage lemma: Let $K_0\subset K_1\subset\cdots$ be full subcategories with union $K_\infty$. If $X$ has finitely many objects, with no restriction on its number of arrows, the canonical comparison is an isomorphism of categories \[ \colim_n\Fun(X,K_n)\longrightarrow\Fun(X,K_\infty), \] and therefore a bijection on components. For an arbitrary filtered diagram of categories the same conclusion holds if $X$ has finitely many arrows. Neither conclusion identifies $\pi_0\Fun(X,K_\infty)$ with $[BX,BK_\infty]$ without an additional argument.
where_proved: sections/E.tex, statement E.2 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 21

statement: V ms.~43 and 46: what fibrant replacement and filtered union supply: An actual sequence $K_n\to K_{n+1}$ admits a strictly commuting map to a sequence of Thomason-fibrant categories $R_n$ with each $K_n\to R_n$ a trivial cofibration. Its induced map of filtered colimits is in $\W_\infty$. Filtered colimits of Thomason-fibrant categories are Thomason-fibrant. In contrast, filtered unions of local categories need not be local, even with finite full stages.
where_proved: sections/E.tex, statement E.3 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 22

statement: V ms.~47--49: an ind-isomorphism need not induce a weak equivalence of unions: There are finite full filtrations $T_0\subset T_1\subset\cdots$, every $T_n$ local and Thomason-fibrant, with fibrant union $T$, and functors $s,\id_T:T\rightrightarrows T$ such that they induce the same morphism of $(T_n)$ in $\Ind(\Cathot)$, but $Bs$ is not a weak equivalence and is not homotopic to the identity. Thus even the additional fibrancy of every stage and both unions does not rescue either the union-isomorphism inference or the uniqueness question of V ms.~47--49.
where_proved: sections/E.tex, statement E.4 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 22
notes: Finite full stages local and fibrant; union fibrant but nonlocal. Independent local-union hypothesis is treated in E.18.

statement: V ms.~48: a local target does not force a strict retract: Even when $A$ is local, $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ is a Thomason cofibration, and a functor $p:B\to A$ satisfies $[p][i]=\id_A$ in $\Cathot$, there need not exist any functor $r:B\to A$ with $ri=\id_A$ as an equality in $\Cat$.
where_proved: sections/E.tex, statement E.5 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 23
notes: Exhaustive 729-map check; target is local but not Thomason-fibrant.

statement: The additional fibrancy version of strict retraction: For a Thomason-fibrant category $A$, a Thomason cofibration $i:A\hookrightarrow B$, and a functor $p:B\to A$ with $[p][i]=\id_A$ in $\Cathot$, this audit does not decide whether some strict retraction $r$ exists in the same $\Cathot$ class as $p$. The finite example in E.5 does not satisfy this extra fibrancy hypothesis.
where_proved: sections/E.tex, statement E.6 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 23
notes: Strict retraction in the same Hot class is proved; preservation of the original Cathot class remains undecided.

statement: V ms.~49--52: categorical homotopy and a canonical mapping object: Stagewise natural-transformation homotopies do not imply a global one, even with full fibrant filtrations, by E.4. Without fibrancy the fence of C.5 realizes the manuscript's proposed unbounded-length mechanism. Fibrancy also does not make every categorical homotopy a single transformation. A canonical replacement for arbitrary relative-category mapping types is a derived mapping space of the simplicial localization, whose components are the localized Hom-sets; this construction has no right adjoint $\Hot\to\Cathot$ as an input.
where_proved: sections/E.tex, statement E.7 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 24

statement: VII ms.~108--124: total categories and actual filtered diagrams: For an actual filtered diagram $D:I\to\Cat$, the canonical map from its Grothendieck construction to $\colim_I D$ is a weak equivalence. Objectwise weak equivalences of actual filtered diagrams induce weak equivalences of colimits. If $P$ has finite CW type, then \[ \colim_i[P,BD_i]\longrightarrow[P,B\colim_iD_i] \] is a bijection. These conclusions do not follow from a mere isomorphism of the diagrams as ind-objects in $\Cathot$ or $\Hot$, and the last assertion is false for a general nerve of a finite category.
where_proved: sections/E.tex, statement E.8 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 24

statement: External Hom in the rectified setting, with its size condition: Suppose a relative category $(\mathcal M,W)$ presents an $\infty$-category $\mathcal C$, and suppose, for every test category $X$ under consideration, its strict diagram localization presents the coherent diagram category: \[ \mathcal M^X[W_X^{-1}]\simeq h\Fun(NX,\mathcal C), \] naturally and compatibly with constant diagrams. Put $Z_{a,b}=\Map_{\mathcal C}(a,b)$. Then \[ \Hom_{\mathcal M^X[W_X^{-1}]}(a_X,b_X) \cong[BX,Z_{a,b}]. \] The derived mapping object $Z_{a,b}$, not a Thomason--Kan envelope, is the correct representing object on $\Hot$. If $\mathcal M$ is $\U$-small and the manuscript's countable path ind-representation holds on all $\Cat_\U$, then this additional rectification assertion on all those shapes forces each $Z_{a,b}$ to be a 1-type.
where_proved: sections/E.tex, statement E.9 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 25
notes: Retains exact diagram-rectification and universe hypotheses.

statement: VII ms.~128--136: strict arrows, strict diagrams, and path types: For every category $C$, the canonical map \[ B\Fun([1],C)\longrightarrow\Map(B[1],BC) \] is a weak equivalence. Its strict fibre at $(a,b)$ need not be a homotopy fibre. For an arbitrary source $Y$, replacing $C$ by a Thomason-fibrant category does not make the corresponding comparison a weak equivalence, and it need not make $\Fun(Y,C)$ fibrant. A corrected mapping-space formula is $\Map_{\mathbf{sSet}}(NY,RNC)$, or the cosimplicial formula of A.5.

statement: VII ms.~127, 150--156 and IX ms.~13: what the set-valued arguments prove: An equality or an inverse verified only in $\Hot_0^{\wedge}$ cannot in general be pulled back to an equality or an inverse in $\Hot$. Thus the finite-test arguments for associativity, $T^2=1$, and weak equivalence of the displayed fibre-transition maps do not prove those conclusions. They are valid statements at the presheaf or ind-object level at which they were established. Fully coherent space-valued finite tests recover the conclusions, and height-two tests detect a specified weak equivalence. Equality of specified maps requires the stronger conditions detailed in Part F. For the actual all-arrows path construction, E.20 and following give direct proofs independent of these invalid inferences.
where_proved: sections/E.tex, statement E.11 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 26

statement: IX ms.~9--13: product-preserving passage and the second psi: The functors $\varphi$, their ind-extensions, restricted Yoneda $R_1^{\mathrm{cat}}$, and filtered-colimit realization in the presheaf category preserve finite products. They preserve the component sets obtained by evaluation at $e$. Therefore composition already specified as a morphism in one of these categories passes forward and gives the same ordinary category on components. The functor $R_1^{\mathrm{cat}}$, called $\psi$ on this page, is neither faithful, full, nor conservative. Its ind-extension is not faithful or full, since these failures already occur on constant ind-objects.
where_proved: sections/E.tex, statement E.12 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 26

statement: IX ms.~10: nonconstant ind-objects can have ordinary colimits in Hot: The assertion that an ind-object of $\Hot$ can have a colimit there only when it is essentially constant is false. The finite discrete spaces $D_n=\{0,\ldots,n\}$ have the discrete countable space $\N$ as colimit in $\Hot$, although $(D_n)$ is not essentially constant in $\Ind(\Hot)$.
where_proved: sections/E.tex, statement E.13 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 27

statement: IX ms.~22--23: the written tests permit a finite nontrivial relative category: There is a finite pointed relative category $(\mathcal E,W)$, whose localization is not equivalent to a point, satisfying the representability tests for $\Sigma,\Omega$, the weak-equivalence invariance of the constant-diagram external Hom, and the displayed higher loop-mapping formulas, when those tests are interpreted exactly as written before the finite-limit hypothesis of IX ms.~24. statement: IX ms.~22--25: representability versus derived loops: In a pointed $\infty$-category $\mathcal C$ having the required finite limits and colimits, define $\Omega b=0\times_b^h0$ and $\Sigma a=0\amalg_a^h0$. There are canonical pointed equivalences \[ \Map_{\mathcal C}(a,\Omega b)\simeq \Omega\Map_{\mathcal C}(a,b)\simeq \Map_{\mathcal C}(\Sigma a,b), \] compatible with loop multiplication. They give $\Sigma\dashv\Omega$ on the homotopy category. In a pointed simplicial model category they can be calculated by replacing $b$ by a fibrant object and factoring its diagonal as \[ b\xrightarrow{\simeq}P b\xrightarrow{(d_0,d_1)}b\times b, \] with the second arrow a fibration, then taking the fibre at the zero pair. The first arrow must be a weak equivalence; merely calling it a cofibration is insufficient.

statement: The scope of the page corrections: Every use of the envelope or of the finite-test inference in the specified ranges is assigned a replacement in the following table. statement: V ms.~44 and 46: local presentations of invariant ind-objects: The following sequential assertion remains unresolved in this audit. Let $K=(K_n)_{n\in\N}$ be a sequence in $\Cathot_\U$, and assume that its associated presheaf \[ H_K(X)=\colim_n\Hom_{\Cathot}(X,K_n) \] sends every map in $\W_\infty$ between $\U$-small categories to a bijection. Must $K$ be isomorphic in $\Ind_\U(\Cathot_\U)$ to a sequence of local categories, equivalently to a sequence of groupoids? The corresponding assertion with an arbitrary $\U$-small filtered indexing category in place of $\N$ also remains unresolved here. We do not infer either assertion from descent in A.7, from the representable-object classification in Part C, or from the obstruction in D.8 for a single represented homotopy type.

W-infinity invariance implies this criterion remains unresolved. Proved for cofinally1-type stages or representable descended presheaf. Enlarged V-small index version is false by D.7.

statement: V ms.~47--49 with genuinely local unions: Let $(K_n)$ and $(K'_n)$ be sequences of full inclusions of $\U$-small categories, with unions $K,K'$. Suppose that the unions themselves are local. Let $u:K\to K'$ be an actual functor carrying each $K_n$ into some $K'_{m(n)}$. If the induced morphism in $\Ind_\U(\Cathot_\U)$ is invertible, then $[u]$ is invertible in $\Cathot$. If two such functors $u,v:K\rightrightarrows K'$ induce the same ind-morphism, then $[u]=[v]$ in $\Cathot$. Localness of the unions is a separate hypothesis here; it does not follow from localness of the stages.
where_proved: sections/E_local_union.tex, statement E.18 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 31

statement: A coherent replacement for arbitrary relative path composition: Let $\mathcal M$ be $\U$-small and let $W$ be a subcategory containing every object. The hammock localization, followed on each mapping simplicial set by $\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}$, gives $\U$-small Kan complexes \[ \mathcal H_W(a,b)=\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty} L^H(\mathcal M,W)(a,b) \qquad(a,b\in\mathcal M) \] with strictly associative, strictly unital simplicial composition. Their component category is canonically $\mathcal M[W^{-1}]$. Precomposition or postcomposition by any specified arrow in $W$ is a weak equivalence of these mapping complexes. These are coherent mapping objects for the relative localization. No comparison with a specified ordinary colimit of the manuscript's path categories is part of this assertion.
where_proved: sections/E_derived.tex, statement E.19 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 32

statement: Finite support and the constant-path equivalence: The constant-path section $j:X\to\mathcal P(X)$ is a weak equivalence. For each $a\in X$, both one-endpoint categories $\mathcal P(X;a,?)$ and $\mathcal P(X;?,a)$ are weakly contractible.

statement: The exact endpoint fibres are homotopy fibres: For each $a,b\in X$, the natural square \[ \begin{array}{ccc} B\mathcal P(X;a,b)&\longrightarrow&B\mathcal P(X)\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow Bp\\ \{(a,b)\}&\longrightarrow&K\times K \end{array} \] is homotopy Cartesian. In particular $B\mathcal P(X;a,b)$ has the weak homotopy type of the ordinary path space $P_{a,b}K$. The comparison with the homotopy fibre is natural for functors over $X\times X$.

statement: The one-sided models and their actual comparison maps: Put $D=(+,-)$. Let $\mathcal L(X)$ be the colimit of the categories of $D^n$-paths under padding by a constant $D$-block on the left, and let $\mathcal R(X)$ use padding on the right. They have constant-path sections and endpoint maps. Their constant-path sections are weak equivalences, their one-endpoint fibres are weakly contractible, and their strict two-endpoint fibres compute their derived endpoint fibres. Constant-tail extension gives functors \[ q_L:\mathcal L(X)\longrightarrow\mathcal P(X), \qquad q_R:\mathcal R(X)\longrightarrow\mathcal P(X) \] which are weak equivalences on total categories and on every fixed-endpoint fibre. These comparisons commute with the canonical path-space comparisons of E.21.
where_proved: sections/E_path.tex, statement E.23 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 35

statement: The manuscript's left-right concatenation is associative: For the block $D=(+,-)$ and $\Sigma=\Mor(X)$, glue a left-half path and a right-half path at their common value at zero. This is an actual functor \[ \kappa:\mathcal L(X)\times_X\mathcal R(X)\longrightarrow\mathcal P(X), \] where the pullback uses the terminal and initial endpoints. On fixed fibres define the manuscript's composition by \[ \mu_{a,b,c}=B\kappa\,\bigl((Bq_L)^{-1}\times(Bq_R)^{-1}\bigr): B\mathcal P(X;a,b)\times B\mathcal P(X;b,c) \longrightarrow B\mathcal P(X;a,c) \quad\hbox{in }\Hot. \] Here the inverses refer to the fixed-fibre weak equivalences of E.23. Under the canonical comparisons to ordinary path spaces, this \emph{particular} operation is ordinary path concatenation. It is therefore associative and unital in $\Hot$; reversal supplies inverses in the usual path-groupoid sense, and the loop object is a group object of $\Hot$.
where_proved: sections/E_path.tex, statement E.24 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 37
notes: The composable-pair category is treated over X cubed; no bare abstract equivalence or finite-test faithfulness is used

statement: Canonical relative collars and literal even translation: For any admissible $\Sigma$, let $\mathcal L_\Sigma(X;a,b)$, $\mathcal R_\Sigma(X;a,b)$, and $\mathcal P_\Sigma(X;a,b)$ be the full relative subcategories of the canonical $D=(+,-)$ models of E.23. The actual constant-tail extension maps $q_L,q_R$ are weak equivalences on these fibres and on their total categories. The literal translation $(T^2c)(j)=c(j-2)$ induces the identity in $\Hot$ on every such fibre. Gluing with the inverses of $q_L,q_R$ consequently defines the canonical relative operation $\mu_D$ in $\Hot$; constant paths are its left and right units.
where_proved: sections/E_path.tex, statement E.25 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 38

statement: The remaining cofinal-type and all-type comparisons: For arbitrary admissible $\Sigma$ and arbitrary left-cofinal projective type sequences as just defined, this audit leaves undecided the following \emph{specified geometric} assertions of VII ms.~108--123: \begin{enumerate} \item A natural transformation $u:t\to t'$ of projective sequences, consisting of strictly commuting maps $u_n:t_n\to t'_n$, always induces a weak equivalence \[ u^*:C_{\infty,\Sigma}(t';a,b)\longrightarrow C_{\infty,\Sigma}(t;a,b). \] \item The isomorphisms obtained from the canonical type projections $t*t'\to t,t'$ are independent of all comparison choices and form the transitive canonical system asserted at ms.~119--123. \item The manuscript's comparison from a sequential colimit to its \emph{all-type} path category is an isomorphism in $\Hot$ for every such relative datum. Precisely, let $E_t$ be the fibred Grothendieck construction of the displayed sequence over $\N^{\op}$ and let $\mathrm{Ch}_\Sigma(X;a,b)\to\mathrm{Ty}$ have fibre $\Fun_\Sigma(I_\tau,X)_{a,b}$. The assertion is that \[ E_t\longrightarrow\mathrm{Ch}_\Sigma(X;a,b) \] is a weak equivalence, so that the span with the ordinary-colimit comparison $E_t\to C_{\infty,\Sigma}(t;a,b)$ yields the claimed isomorphism. \end{enumerate}

statement: The remaining relative and arbitrary-block composition assertions: Fix an admissible $\Sigma$ and a word $\tau_0$ with $\ell_u(\tau_0)\geq2$. Form the three actual systems of VII ms.~125--126: the stages $\tau_0^n$ with transitions which collapse only the extra left blocks, the stages $\tau_0^n$ with transitions which collapse only the extra right blocks, and the stages $\tau_0^{2n}$ with symmetric outer collapse. Denote their colimits by $L_{\tau_0,\Sigma}$, $R_{\tau_0,\Sigma}$, and $P_{\tau_0,\Sigma}$, with endpoints understood. Constant padding defines actual maps $q_L:L_{\tau_0,\Sigma}\to P_{\tau_0,\Sigma}$ and $q_R:R_{\tau_0,\Sigma}\to P_{\tau_0,\Sigma}$, and concatenation defines the actual gluing functor $\kappa_{\tau_0}$. Beyond E.24--E.25, the audit does not settle all of the following claims of ms.~125--127: both padding maps are weak equivalences for every block; the resulting operations $\kappa_{\tau_0}(q_L^{-1}\times q_R^{-1})$ are independent of the block under the specified comparison maps; and those operations are associative in $\Hot$ for every admissible $\Sigma$.

statement: The two relevant finiteness conditions: Every finite CW homotopy type is represented by a finite poset. A category with finitely many arrows has a nerve with a finite $2$-skeleton, so each component of its classifying space has finitely presented fundamental group. Its nerve need not be homotopy equivalent to a finite CW complex. In particular the one-object category $BC_2$, with arrows $1,g$ and $g^2=1$, is finite, whereas $B(BC_2)$ is not a compact object of $\Spc$.

There is a single endomorphism $s_B:BG\to BG$ such that $s_B\ne\id_{BG}$, $s_B$ is not an isomorphism in $\Hot$, and both restricted functors send it to the identity.

statement: Fullness of finite set-valued tests: The functors $R_1^{\mathrm{cat}}$ and $R_1^{\mathrm{fin}}$ are not full. This is a separate failure from F.2: there are natural transformations between their values which are not induced by any morphism in $\Hot$.

In particular no such set jointly reflects isomorphisms or separates all morphisms.

statement: The stronger nonconcreteness obstruction: The category $\Hot$ admits no faithful functor to $\Set_{\U}$ with the usual fixed-universe interpretation. The obstruction already occurs on simply connected, finite-dimensional CW complexes. Therefore faithfulness of a restricted set-valued Yoneda functor cannot be obtained by substituting any other $\U$-small full test subcategory.

If $T_r$ denotes the $r$th finite subtelescope, the canonical map $(T_r)_r\to T$ in $\Ind(\Hot)$ is not an epimorphism.

statement: The exact Ind-completion assertion: In the fixed universe there is an equivalence \[ \Ind_{\omega}(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{fin}})\simeq\Spc \] whose restriction to $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{fin}}$ is its given inclusion. Thus \[ R_{\infty}^{\mathrm{fin}}:\Spc\longrightarrow \Fun(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{fin}}^{\op},\Spc), \qquad X\longmapsto\Map(-,X)|_{\mathcal A_{\mathrm{fin}}} \] is fully faithful. The compact objects of $\Spc$ are exactly the retracts in $\Spc$ of finite CW homotopy types; no assertion that all such retracts have finite CW type is needed.

statement: Finite-category space-valued tests are dense, but are not all compact: The functor \[ R_{\infty}^{\mathrm{cat}}:\Spc\longrightarrow \Fun(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{cat}}^{\op},\Spc) \] is fully faithful. Nevertheless the filtered-colimit extension $\Ind_{\omega}(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{cat}})\to\Spc$ of the inclusion is not an equivalence. Thus ``spaces are the Ind-completion of finite spaces'' proves the intended positive statement only after specifying finite CW homotopy types, or their retract completion, as the compact generators.

statement: Conservativity returns at height two: For every integer $n\geq2$, both $R_n^{\mathrm{fin}}$ and $R_n^{\mathrm{cat}}$ reflect equivalences. In fact a map $f:X\to Y$ is a weak equivalence if \[ \Pi_1\Map(S^r,f):\Pi_1\Map(S^r,X) \longrightarrow\Pi_1\Map(S^r,Y) \] is an equivalence of groupoids for every $r\geq0$.

statement: Faithfulness at the highest retained dimension: For every finite $n\geq1$, neither $R_n^{\mathrm{fin}}$ nor $R_n^{\mathrm{cat}}$ is faithful on the highest retained morphisms. More precisely, for $T$ from F.6, $Y_n=K(\Z,n+1)$, and the constant map $0:T\to Y_n$, the comparison on $\pi_{n-1}$ of mapping spaces has a nonzero kernel. For $n=1$ this means the map on components. Consequently these functors are not fully faithful as $n$-functors for any finite $n$.

notes: Nonzero alpha in H^2(T;Z)=pi_(n-1) Map(T,K(Z,n+1)) is invisible; n=2 gives phantom homotopy.

statement: A precise gain for countable sources: Let $X$ have countable CW homotopy type, let $Y$ be any $\U$-small space, let $n\geq1$, and use finite CW tests. The canonical map \[ \theta_n:\tau_{\leq n-1}\Map(X,Y) \longrightarrow \Map_{\mathcal P_{n-1}(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{fin}})} (R_n^{\mathrm{fin}}X,R_n^{\mathrm{fin}}Y) \] is surjective on components. It induces isomorphisms on $\pi_k$ for $0\leq k<n-1$ and surjections on $\pi_{n-1}$, with basepoints wherever required. In particular coherent height-two finite CW tests determine equality of homotopy classes of maps with countable CW source. The same conclusion about equality holds if one is given coherent tests on all finite-category homotopy types.
where_proved: sections/F.tex, statement F.11 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 47
notes: Statement restricted to countable CW sources; no arbitrary-source transfer.

statement: Ordinary fullness and faithfulness at every finite height: For every finite $n\geq2$, neither $hR_n^{\mathrm{fin}}$ nor $hR_n^{\mathrm{cat}}$ is full or faithful on the ordinary sets of homotopy classes of maps. Nonfaithfulness has examples whose source has CW cardinality $\aleph_{n-1}$; nonfullness has examples whose source has CW cardinality $\aleph_n$. Moreover, for each $0\leq k\leq n-1$, the map on the retained $\pi_k$ of a mapping space can fail to be injective. All the groups, modules, and spaces in these examples are $\U$-small.

notes: Locally finite abelian G of cardinal aleph_(n-1) and rational twisted K(M,n) sections refute faithfulness; cardinal aleph_n and nonsplit K(M,n) fibration refute fullness. Every retained pi_k can fail injectivity. Modules obtained from U-small bar syzygies.

statement: What testing can justify for composition and reversal: Let $P$ be a space with a specified morphism $m:P\times P\to P$ in $\Hot$, and let $T:P\to P$ be a specified endomorphism. Equality of the two associativity composites, or of $T^2$ and $\id_P$, does not follow in general from equality after every finite set-valued test. For each fixed finite height there are actual operations and endomorphisms for which the corresponding coherent finite-test identities hold but these identities in $\Hot$ fail. A coherent homotopy of their space-valued finite-test natural transformations does imply the corresponding equality in $\Hot$. A coherent height-two finite-test homotopy suffices when the source of the proposed equality has countable CW homotopy type. For arbitrary sources no fixed finite height supplies a general equality criterion: F.12 gives distinct ordinary homotopy classes with coherently identical finite tests at every prescribed finite height.
where_proved: sections/F.tex, statement F.13 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 51
notes: Literal false positives: fibrewise translation T by nonzero rational cohomology section has R_n T=id but T^2!=id; m=T pr_1 is not associative though its coherent finite-height tests are. Does not claim any particular path model fails.

statement: Finite posets and necessary finiteness conditions: A homotopy type is the classifying-space type of a finite poset if and only if it has a finite CW model. Every homotopy type with a finite CW model consequently has a finite categorical model. For any finite category $C$, $BC$ has finitely many cells in each dimension, finitely many components, finitely presented fundamental groups, and finitely generated integral homology in every degree. These latter conditions do not imply that $BC$ has a finite CW model.
where_proved: sections/G.tex, statement G.1 and following proof/discussion; PDF p. 52

statement: Finite type is not sufficient for finite categorical realization: The assertion that every simply connected homotopy type with a simplicial model finite in every degree has a finite categorical model is false.

statement: Unrestricted monoids and countable models: Every connected CW homotopy type is the classifying-space type of a small discrete monoid. For a connected countable CW homotopy type the monoid can be chosen countable.

statement: A finite monoid cannot have a nonsimply connected finite-dimensional type: Let $M$ be a finite monoid. Its universal group $U(M)=\pi_1(BM)$ is finite. If $BM$ is homotopy equivalent to a finite-dimensional CW complex, then $U(M)=1$. In particular neither $S^1$ nor $\mathbb{RP}^2$ is the classifying-space type of a finite monoid.

The global arrow minimum $a_{\mathrm{pos}}(\mathbb{RP}^2)$ satisfies \[ 28\leq a_{\mathrm{pos}}(\mathbb{RP}^2)\leq49. \] We do not identify that global minimum.
